CANONICAL_NAME.value: ELIZA in BBN-LISP (1969, revised 1972) -- Bernie Cosell's independent implementation at BBN

ERA.value: 1969 (body: the file is dated 1969 and 1972 by its own name and content)

value.lineage: Bernie Cosell wrote an ELIZA independently at BBN in LISP, having read the CACM description rather than the code. A SECOND, independent organism solving the same problem in a different language and a different world -- BBN-LISP on a PDP-10 rather than MAD-SLIP on a 7094 under CTSS. Its behaviour and structure are therefore an independent answer to the same pressure, not a port.

value.pressure: reconstructing behaviour from a paper rather than from source; a different machine and language

cut.note: an ELIZA written from the CACM paper, not the code: the reader splits input into sentences and keeps a KEYSTACK of keywords ranked by a PRIORITY property; the sentence with the highest-priority keyword is the one analysed; a MEMORY stack holds transformations to use when no keyword fires; the body is the 1969 printout plus a 1972 revision, wrapped in a compatibility package that re-creates BBN-LISP's semantics (optional arguments filled with NIL, CDR of a symbol as its property list, TCONC) so the original text runs unaltered

organs.human_name: MAKESENTENCE (441-500): RATOM word loop; TRMLIS ends input; PCTLIS starts a new sentence; on a new sentence the KEYSTACKs are compared by (GETP ... PRIORITY) and the higher one wins; DOCTOR (395-440): the loop, GOODBYE, the elapsed-time sign-off
organs.mechanism: words are read one at a time; numbers are packed with a marker; a terminal symbol ends the input; punctuation ends a sentence and recursively reads the next; when two sentences exist the one whose keyword stack's top has the greater PRIORITY property survives (the other is dropped), which is the paper's rule that only one sentence is answered; the doctor loop prints a prompt, builds a sentence, exits on GOODBYE with the session length in minutes, else calls ANALYZE
organs.output: one sentence and its keyword stack
assumptions: keywords carry a numeric priority on their property list (the script sets it); one sentence per turn is enough
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the selection of WHICH sentence to answer is done at read time, before any matching
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: priority ties resolve to the earlier sentence; a sentence with no keyword is answered from MEMORY or with a none-response (SETNONE)
organs.human_prior: Weizenbaum 1966 CACM (the keyword ranking); this is an independent implementation of the paper's description

organs.human_name: ANALYZE (503-545), TEST / TEST4 / ADVANCE (546-620: the decomposition matcher over the keyword's rule list), RECONSTRUCT (620-670: reassembly and printing), MEMORY (669-688), SETNONE (715-751)
organs.mechanism: for the top keyword, its rules are tried in order; a decomposition pattern is matched against the sentence by a segment matcher (TEST/TEST4 advance through the sentence, ADVANCE moves the pattern); on success one reassembly rule is chosen by rotating a pointer (RPLQQ rotates the rule list in place so successive uses cycle) and RECONSTRUCT substitutes the captured segments and prints; certain keywords also push a transformed sentence onto MEMORY; when no keyword matches, a memory entry is popped, else a content-free response is given
assumptions: the paper's decomposition/reassembly scheme; rotation of the rule list is the cheapest way to avoid repeating a response
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the second, independent ELIZA; behaviour reproduced from prose alone
organs.source_boundary: the 1969 DOCFNS beyond MAKESENTENCE; CANDIDATE because bodies were skimmed

organs.human_name: package :bbn-lisp (70-345): DEFINEQ with optional arguments filled with NIL, CDR of a symbol as its plist, TCONC, PUT/GETP, the readtables for the patient's input; the transcription notes (1-65)
organs.mechanism: rather than editing the printout, the transcribers wrote a package that shadows the Common Lisp symbols whose 1969 semantics differ (CONS with no arguments, CDR/RPLACD on symbols, NLAMBDA as a macro, optional arguments) and a reader for the patient's punctuation; the 1969 and 1972 codes are loaded into separate packages with separate scripts
assumptions: preserving the artifact matters more than idiomatic code; the differences between dialects are enumerable
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the original bytes are the body; every deviation is in one place and documented
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the TODO list names three unresolved semantics (CLOCK in 1972, nlistp, MEMB vs member)
organs.human_prior: the same discipline this atlas calls C9 (faithful branch first)

pressures.source_evidence: MAKESENTENCE's priority comparison; RPLQQ; MEMORY; the transcript file
pressures.condition: an organism receives multi-sentence input; it has a table of keywords with priorities and rules; the score is a human's willingness to continue and the absence of verbatim repetition; the organism has no model of meaning
pressures.resource_or_constraint: a small script; a memory stack
pressures.failure_condition: answering the wrong sentence, repeating a response, or silence when no keyword fires
pressures.world_punishes: first-sentence-always; a fixed reassembly per rule; no memory
pressures.world_rewards: priority selection at read time, rotation of reassembly rules, a memory stack
pressures.observable_consequence: transcript length and repetition count with human subjects (the body ships a 1969 transcript) for the priority rule vs first-sentence and rotation vs fixed
pressures.cheat_control: an organism given the human's next line must be indistinguishable from the transcript; first-sentence-always must answer the wrong sentence on the transcript's multi-sentence inputs; rotation off must repeat within the transcript's length: the world must show all three
